entities.name: Lothar I. von Stade
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Lothar I, Count of Stade, played a significant role in shaping the medieval political landscape of the Holy Roman Empire.

Born around 840, Lothar I ascended to the throne in 855 after the death of his father, Louis the German, and his half-brother, Charles the Bald. He ruled as the Count of Stade, a powerful noble family in the Duchy of Saxony, and worked to strengthen the empire's borders against the Viking raids and Slavic invasions.

Lothar I's strategic alliances and military campaigns helped to secure the empire's territories and expand its influence in the region. He also played a key role in the establishment of the Treaty of Verdun in 843, which divided the Carolingian Empire among his three sons, Louis the German, Charles the Bald, and Lothair I.

Despite his significant contributions to the empire's stability, Lothar I's legacy is often overshadowed by that of his more famous contemporaries. Nevertheless, his efforts to strengthen the empire's defenses and promote the interests of the Saxon nobility remain an important chapter in the history of medieval Germany.

The 880s saw the rise of the Ottonian dynasty, which would go on to shape the course of German history for centuries to come. Lothar I's son, Louis the Younger, would eventually succeed him as Count of Stade and play a key role in the Ottonian dynasty's rise to power.
